title: Introduce haptic-informed radius and spectral swatch mapping for token library
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Summary: Define and add a small orthogonal expansion of the token library that does three things: (1) introduces a spectral swatch mapping for semantic overlays and interactive accents (to reduce color friction across charts, alerts, and badges), (2) defines a compact set of haptic-informed radius tokens tuned for touch and desktop affordances, and (3) provides motion/tilt-aware elevation presets (shadow primitives) to support subtle motion-responsive surfaces in product animations. Goal: improve perceptual consistency across density modes, reduce visual jank when model-driven content changes, and provide a migration path for existing components to the new token names. Rationale: current token set mixes semantic palettes and legacy named neutrals; radius scale is large-grained for mobile vs desktop; shadow steps are not tuned for motion nor for overlapping layered surfaces. Deliverables: token spec doc, figma kit update, token JSON (light/dark) with mapping table, migration adapter script, QA checklist, and a short rollout plan for components library and docs.
acceptance_criteria: A canonical token JSON (light & dark) is published with new spectral swatch keys and a compact radius.touch.* scale (xs/s/m/l) documented
Figma components updated and validated: buttons, table rows, cards, toasts, badge variants use spectral swatch variables rather than legacy hard-coded colors
Migration adapter script (node) translates legacy token names to new keys and includes a dry-run mode; results validated by Design and Eng
Motion library demonstrates tilt-reactive elevation presets for at least 3 components (card, floating menu, toast) with performance budget <8ms per frame at 60fps in prototype
Accessibility review: contrast ratios for semantic overlays meet AA for body text or provide explicit exception notes where decorative only
Rollout notes and deprecation window published; no production component is left referencing legacy tokens past the stated deprecation date without an approved exception
rollout_plan: Week 1: Finalize token names and JSON schemas; publish spec to Confluence; push figma kit update
Week 2: Run migration script across a sample of components in the monorepo; open PRs with token substitutions (design + eng review)
Week 3: QA and accessibility sweep; iterate on color deltas and elevation values based on results
Week 4: Official release of token package; begin deprecation notices for legacy tokens; schedule follow-up grooming for remaining components
migration_steps: 1) Export current token map and generate mapping table to new keys (legacy -> spectral/radius/elevation)
2) Run migration-adapter.js in dry-run mode to generate a changelist and affected component list
3) Triage high-traffic components and ship PRs in small batches (buttons -> tables -> alerts -> charts)
4) Monitor dashboards for visual regressions (console visual-diff job + sampling in staging)
5) After 4 weeks, mark legacy tokens deprecated and add linter rule to warn on legacy usage
qa_checks: Visual diff: all changed components must have < 1% pixel delta threshold on critical views
Contrast: semantic overlay combinations report pass/fail; any failures require documented use-case justification
Performance: prototype shadows should not add synchronous repaint cost; run Lighthouse check on interactive demo
Touch targets: verify radius.touch.* preserves minimum hit target visuals and does not reduce affordance
Token API: ensure tokens load in both light/dark and with reduced-motion/user-preference overrides
notes: Token naming convention proposal: spectral.[role].[tint] (e.g., spectral.success.40) and radius.touch.{xs,sm,md,lg}
Elevation primitives: elevation.motion.{low,mid,high} to pair with reduced-motion user preference; the motion variants add subtle offset and blur changes keyed to tilt/scroll events
We will not change chart color ramps in this pass; instead chart palettes will map to spectral anchors to avoid rebaseline churn
Design test: run small sampled user study internally with product designers to confirm perceived depth and touch comfort
